newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares firmer in early bourse dealings.
newsitem.headline: German shares firmer in early bourse dealings.

text.p: German shares were firmer in early bourse dealings on Tuesday as the DAX index of bourse trade caught up with its electronic IBIS counterpart on the strong dollar and an overnight Wall Street advance.

The 30-share DAX index was up 21.19 points, or 0.63 percent, at 3,384.25 in early bourse, while the IBIS DAX index, which reflects all-day electronic trade, was up 10.19 points, or 0.30 percent, at 3,383.15.
"Despite the relatively friendly influence from Wall Street, the German market is rather sluggish," SuedwestLB said in its morning market commentary.
Traders looked for the DAX index to remain within a range from 3,360 to 3,400 points for the session and also possibly on Wednesday ahead of Thursday's market holiday.

But some said the DAX could break the psychologically important 3,400 level during the week and keep up the advance led by dollar-sensitive shares, particularly carmakers, if volumes were to return to the market.
"A lot will depend on when institutional investors return to the market and we can shake off this lethargic feeling," said one trader, noting the lack of fresh market orders.

Among specific shares, ball-bearings maker Kugelfischer AG was one of the top percentage gainers, rising 60 pfennigs to 31.20 marks after reporting higher 1996 profits, before paring gains to stand at 31 marks later on.
Industrial group Daimler-Benz AG was up 55 pfennigs at 127.30 marks ahead of its public introduction today in Frankfurt of its new A-class compact vehicle.
Chemicals group Degussa AG was down 40 pfennigs at 78.70 marks, despite reporting a 25 percent gain in first half profits and giving an optimistic outlook for the second half.
The share hit a new high of 81.25 marks in electronic trade, but traders said that while the earnings outlook was good the sales were at the lower end of expectations.
"Selling on good news" was also a factor, traders said.
